draft.title: Business plans and borrowing
card: A business plan sets out a business's goals and how it will reach them. It can cover the product, customers, costs and expected income.
Many businesses need to borrow money to start or to grow. Lenders, such as banks, are the ones who lend it.
Lenders read the business plan before lending. It helps them judge whether the business is likely to earn enough to repay the loan.
A loan must be paid back, and the lender usually charges interest on top.
draft.remember: A business plan shows a lender where the business is headed and how it can repay a loan.

a.q: Why would a bank ask to read a business plan before lending money?
opts: To judge if the business can repay the loan
To decide which products customers will buy
To choose the name for the business
To set the prices the business will charge
a.why: The plan shows the goals and expected income, so the bank can judge if the loan will be repaid. The bank does not run the business, so it does not choose products, names or prices.
a.clue: Think about what a lender wants back.

b.q: Priya wants a loan to open a bakery in Darwin. Which should she do first to help the bank decide?
opts: Write a plan with goals, costs and expected income
Ask the bank to write the plan for her
Open the bakery and show the bank later
Tell the bank she will repay it somehow
b.why: A plan with goals, costs and expected income gives the bank what it reads before lending. Saying she will repay it somehow gives the bank nothing to judge, so it is the weaker choice.
b.clue: What would the bank want to read?

a.best: To judge if the business can repay the loan

b.best: Write a plan with goals, costs and expected income

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a precise detail (goals, costs and expected income), echoing the card's list. A student could pick it by matching words without understanding why lenders read plans.

The why calls 'Tell the bank she will repay it somehow' 'the weaker choice'. That suggests it is partly right, when it is simply wrong. It should say this gives the bank nothing to judge, so it does not help.

b.q: Priya wants a loan to open a bakery in Darwin. Which would help the bank judge whether she can repay it?
opts: A plan showing how her sales could cover repayments
A written promise that she will repay the loan
Drawings of how she will decorate the shop
Proof she has already chosen a name for the bakery
b.why: The bank wants to know if the bakery is likely to earn enough to repay the loan, and a plan shows how her sales could do that. A promise to repay gives the bank nothing to judge, so it does not help. Decorations and a name say nothing about income.
b.clue: The bank needs evidence, not just words.
